commits.author: penfever
commits.message:
[sft] Express the Exp3 V5 mix as an artifact graph (#11658)

Express the exact SFT mix Exp3 trained on as a Marin artifact graph, so
a run's
mix is recoverable from its records.

Exp3's production SFT stage (job
`/benfeuer/long-loop-exp3-2026.11.16.51`) consumed
data release V5 (`release-complete-v5.json`, SHA-256 `3e216194…`).
Coordinator
sign-off `450bc8a4b24613c6b6f00e07da9b3953` approved that exact URI and
digest, and
the run's consumed data config equals the release's `data.json` on every
release
field; the launcher added only default-valued fields.

`experiments/sft_new_mix/exp3_v5_mix.py` defines that mix as versioned
handles:

- The release document and its cache catalog are adopted at their exact
URIs, with
  the pinned SHA-256 digests recorded in the handle configs.
- Each of the 434 sources is a `TokenizedCache` seal step whose
fingerprinted config
pins the digest of the source's cache-catalog entry — the ledger that
carries the
source's exact content-addressed shard caches — plus its row and token
counts,
shard count, and loss mode (384 full-token replay sources, 50
assistant-only chat
sources, one teacher-only relay source). No data is copied or
recomputed.
- `exp3_v5_data_config()` assembles the `LmDataConfig` through
`mixture()`: the
natural weights in the release's three-phase schedule (boundaries
0/250/500),
full-permutation feistel shuffle, the release cache catalog, and the
seven
8-sequence IID validation reservations. A test resolves the graph
offline and pins
the resolved config component by component against
`fixtures/exp3_v5_data.json`,
  whose content is the release member the run consumed.
- `exp3_v5_seal_check()` verifies the seal before a consumer uses the
mix: the
catalog digest, every source's entry digest and counts, and that all
1,900
  content-addressed shard caches exist.

`TokenizedCache` now reads a sealed cache's recorded cache dir, prebuilt
format, and
packing, so `mixture()` can consume a cache registered beside a manifest
rather than
beside its data.

One consumed-config field is recorded as provenance and is not part of
the resolved
components: bounded-lookahead packing (cap 256, lookahead 128) was a
property of the
Exp3 training runtime. A consumer packs with its own policy.

Rebuilding the mix from sources would need these transforms as
fingerprinted variant
steps:

- Chat conversion and loss masking for the 50 chat sources from pinned
`DatakitChatSource` pipelines (assistant-only masks, relay
teacher-only), plus
full-token masking and scripted tokenization for the 384 replay sources
  (`scripted-v3`, `scripted-v4-remainder`, `scripted-ranges-v5`).
- Replay line restoration (`replay-line-restoration-v1`, 20,707 restored
context
  IDs).
- Quality gates (`gate-high-science-v1`, `gate-math-rest-v1`) with their
pinned
  calibration evidence.
- Atlas drops (`atlas-applied-v5`: 1,429 exact duplicates and 8,520
lexical flags)
  using the release's bloom and population pins.
- OpenCode raw-question repair (`opencode-raw-question-repaired-v1`:
409,004
  repaired rows) using the release's bridge and index pins.

Each variant step needs a typed config whose fingerprint covers the
source pin and
the transform's pinned inputs (label tables, gate calibrations, and
Atlas
references, each by digest). The post-EOT newline repair is not part of
this mix;
it belongs to the separate V6 candidate, which Exp3 did not train on. No
rebuild
ran, and the sealed caches remain the training inputs.


Design note from review: the seal records and the seal-check config are
release-literal
JSON dicts, fingerprinted exactly as recorded. The release document is
the schema of
record — the pin is the point — so wrapping them in dataclasses would
fork the recorded
identity without adding a contract the pinned release does not already
carry.


Unrelated to the mix, this PR also repairs
`test_fa4_attention_traces_through_hero_loss_and_gradient` for CPU-only
runners — since #11543 the QB loss path calls the cached `gpu_family()`
helper, which probes `jax.devices("gpu")` under the test's stubbed `gpu`
backend, so the test now stubs `jax.devices` with an H100-like device
and clears the gpu-family caches per that helper's documented contract.

commits.author: chrismc91
commits.message:
[eval] Grade on the task machines' backend (#12283)

An evaluation run's graders now run on the same backend as its task
machines. Before, a worker without an explicit verifier machine always
graded in its local sandbox (bubblewrap on the Iris worker), so
benchmarks whose package tests grade in a separate verifier machine,
such as SWE-bench-Science, applied and executed the agent's changes on
the worker even when the task machines were on Daytona, and pulled each
task's verifier image there. The default verifier machine stays
network-denied; runs without task machines grade locally, and an
explicit `verifier_machine` still wins.

Judged graders and graders that run in the agent's own machine are
unaffected: neither uses the verifier machine. SWE-bench-Science smokes
graded on Daytona this way (96 tasks, two models) with no grading
failures attributable to placement.

commits.author: atqamar
commits.message:
[rl] Run nightly controls and gate by preset version (#12187)

The nightly workflow requests at least one main control per gated preset across seven control series. It adds runs when fewer than five controls have completed at the current version. Snowball controls use Reno H100s. Mochi controls fit within one 60-GB200 NVLink domain. Snowball `data-medium` runs ungated and reports evaluation scores. `learning-medium` owns the shared default configuration's control cohort.

The gate selects the five latest eligible main controls at the branch's base preset version. Marina history uses the same eligibility selector. The archived model command derives that version by hashing the effective native launch configuration. The gate reports the base version and count when a cohort is short. Both scheduled jobs route failures to the nightly report.

A manual dispatch on `main` can select several models or gated presets. A commenter with repository write access can use `/rl-controls snowball/learning-medium mochi` on a merged PR to dispatch those controls from `main` and receive the run link. The controls job checks for the main branch of `marin-community/marin` before checkout and cloud authentication.

The controls job configures the main-only `marin-cd-cloud-run-deploy` identity for Marina index reads and publication. Iris and GCS keep the `github-iris` identity.

The recorded Snowball speed-medium run passed with no change against five controls at `ec834775`. Mochi learning-medium passed with improvement against five controls at `9d23aea1`, with 100/100 tasks scored on both panels. The Mochi candidate’s final family mean was 0.82415 versus 0.73354 across its controls. These branch comparisons published to isolated Marina. Hosted publication requires a Marina runtime with the shared record schema.

[Snowball dispatch](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/45582327170) · [Snowball candidate](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fatqamar%2Fusers-ahmad-checkpoints-snowball-rl-speed-medium-506a9fd43c-in-8037ac9b-gate-n1-defaults-11c8349f-controls-15b9459e-evidence-7a90a1bf-2026.11.25-coordinator-b7a1002d) · [Mochi speed dispatch](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/45605698440) · [Mochi learning dispatch](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/45630885257) · [Mochi candidate](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fatqamar%2Fusers-ahmad-checkpoints-mochi-rl-learning-medium-3ded2363f7-in-d8b267c9-gate-n1-defaults-0b2f5d64-controls-c684c4aa-evidence-aa117e87-2026.11.25-coordinator-48b4aa63)

commits.author: atqamar
commits.message:
[rl] Chart control history and link EvalDash to RL attempts (#12188)

For each preset, Marina charts final scores from the latest successful control attempt per run output on clean main. The comparable line joins consecutive scores with matching task sets, evaluation settings, and scored answer indices. Family scores also compare task-family assignments. The global line connects all plotted control scores. A toggle shows branch runs at their recorded attempt times.

Each point opens its exact attempt and its recorded links, verdict, source provenance, redacted settings, and launch configuration. Marina uses the run’s preset version for a clean main control at the merge base. For other runs, the model command in the merge-base archive supplies the base preset version when available. EvalDash links exported-policy evaluations with stored run and attempt IDs to the corresponding Marina attempt.

Selection manifests record catalog source IDs for training and evaluation subsets. Gate reports check task IDs and answers per task against the recorded launch. When the preset requires coverage, the report also checks the share of tasks with a scored answer.

Part of #12186.

commits.author: atqamar
commits.message:
[rl] Index Snowball and Mochi runs in Marina (#12186)

Marina indexes prepared and terminal attempts from Snowball and Mochi preset runs. A watcher on the launching host follows detached runs and uses stored run and control receipts to locate any required gate report.

Marina and Grafana share the run ID that W&B uses to group attempts. W&B defaults to `marin-rl` and tags attempts with the model, preset, preset version, user, and branch when known. Grafana links use the recorded native Iris job and execution window when available.

The index sums trainer time excluding evaluation when every attempt in the checkpoint lineage has trainer timing and a native job window. `--plan` reports control pin checks for gated candidates. Use `publish --issue` with `--run-output` and `--attempt` to associate a stored terminal or interrupted attempt with a GitHub issue.

commits.author: atqamar
commits.message:
[rl] Use checked-in SkyRL launch and gate entry points (#12195)

The SkyRL launcher and candidate checks use the checked-in native entry points. GPU jobs run the PyTorch transport probe. For a single NVLink domain, every rank must show a full-world NVLS communicator or a cross-host MNNVL channel during the benchmark. Training probes also check vLLM’s PyNccl initialization. Jobs that publish to the Hugging Face Hub use the CPU profile of the shared setup hook. Bootstrap writes the environment as data for node and nightly processes. The controller prepares Ray spill storage before starting Ray.

One CPU supervisor serves the SkyRL launcher, the gate, and native test fixtures. It captures diagnostics and terminates the whole process group on timeout or failure. The gate uses the vendored CLI to compose launch documents, validate driver settings, and read schema defaults. Frozen environment preparation has a 300-second budget and the native CLI has a separate 120-second budget. A stage file records the current operation for redacted failure reports.

CI selects each affected test file once per suite.

The dataset reader takes missing task labels from the selection manifest and checks every non-null stored label against it.

The P104 Reno training proof at `32eaeee8b2` passed transport checks, started Ray, and wrote a step-1 checkpoint on 40 H100s. Its export converted the checkpoint on 32 H100s and verified the Hugging Face files in object storage. [Training proof](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fatqamar%2Fusers-ahmad-checkpoints-snowball-rl-p104-train-20261125-2026.11.22.3-ad68fefc69f5) · [Export proof](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fatqamar%2Fatqamar-p104-export-fresh-20261125)

The X1 Mochi startup proof on the integrated head `386863e4a2` passed the transport probe and verified 15 Ray hosts within one healthy NVLink fabric. [Mochi startup proof](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/45605698440)

The native EvalLite reader test passed with a nullable label and an explicit conflict. On the stored quick and full panels, task digests and non-null labels all agreed with the manifest.

commits.author: atqamar
commits.message:
[rl] Reduce Snowball train-long memory and isolate run state (#11943)

Snowball `train-long` packs samples and uses two context-parallel ranks with KV all-gather for both policy and reference. A 25-update Reno proof completed all updates on 40 H100s with this memory configuration. The CP1 run exhausted memory in update 24. [Memory proof](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin-snowball-rl/runs/ad32076d128a)

Published task selections are read-only inputs. The runner checks that the selection exists without writing registration or execution metadata. Launcher NCCL rendezvous is scoped to the Iris job and attempt. The gate estimates GPU-hours using the configured GPU count and the time from the first recorded workload start to native job completion.

commits.message:
[skyrl] Keep only the NVLink fabric check in the placement audit (#12265)

Every node of a locality group must still report the same healthy
cluster-UUID/clique-ID pair before model actors start. The
distinct-host, complete-rank-coverage and rank/locality-label-agreement
checks are dropped, and the audit now groups nodes by their observed
locality label. The report still persists each node's rank, host, group
and fabric, and the audit still requires the expected number of alive
Ray nodes.

Kueue already places each model group inside one NVLink domain, and the
placement half of the audit had no observed failure to catch. The fabric
half is the cross-host comparison that catches the incident-898 failure
mode, where a node dropped out of its NVLink domain while Kueue still
placed the group on that rack (https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/898).

Follow-up to #11807, from the review thread asking to drop the placement
checks and keep the fabric verification.

[tests] Make misleading tests check what their names claim (#12347)

Make eleven tests fail when the behavior they are named for breaks. Each
one could pass with the code wrong: its assertion was satisfied by any
input, it checked only log or status text, or it had no assertion at
all. This continues #10883.

-
`lib/verifyit/tests/test_judge.py::test_pairwise_verdict_takes_last_match_of_first_matching_pattern`:
every row expected reward 0.5, which any recognised verdict produces, so
the test could not tell which match won. It now asserts the parsed
verdict for each game, and the double-bracket preference case is a row
of the same table.
- `lib/iris/tests/cluster/controller/test_observability_rows.py`:
`test_failed_write_commits_and_runs_later_post_commit_hooks` now checks
that the submitted job exists after a failed row write.
`test_slow_rows_are_logged_and_counted_in_the_dbs_lock_cost` is deleted:
it asserted only warning text, and the lock-cost record is already
checked by
`test_a_submit_emits_one_row_record_after_releasing_the_lock`. In
`test_every_cluster_config_forwards_under_its_own_name_or_not_at_all`,
configs without a Finelog config used to pass through a bare `return`;
the parameter list now holds only configs that set one.
-
`experiments/post_training/rl_tests/test_runner_models.py::test_mochi_agentic_plan_collects_attempts_with_exports_disabled`
asserted human status text and never checked exports. It now parses the
plan status, checks that attempt collection is planned for the run, and
checks the composed launch config has `export_hf` False.
`printed_status` moved into `rl_tests/fixtures.py` so both test modules
share it.
- `lib/taskcompendium/tests/test_evalchemy_code.py`: two CRUX tests only
executed the program with no assertion, and a third pinned
`SyntaxError`. Their cases are now rows of
`test_crux_reads_answers_by_the_harness_rule`, which asserts pass or

-
`tests/sft/test_hf_to_levanter.py::test_sft_exports_once_at_the_final_update`
also checked model resolution; those checks are now two named tests:
`test_sft_model_resolves_to_the_final_update_export` and

-
`experiments/post_training/task_curation/tests/test_lean.py::test_the_proofnet_eval_is_left_out_of_default_campaigns`
asserted the checked-in declaration type; it now runs the driver's
source selection and checks ProofNet is excluded by default and included

-
`experiments/post_training/task_curation/tests/test_daytona_identity.py`:
the two `machine_spec` tests asserted that supplied values came back;
one parametrized test now checks the real mapping from `allow_internet`
to the network policy.
-
`test_no_oracle_qualification.py::test_a_faithful_mode_change_is_reported_not_failed`
and `lib/rigging/tests/test_network.py` now pin the exact octal mode
report and the address in the error, so a decimal-parsed mode or a

No product bugs turned up. Not run locally:
`tests/sft/test_hf_to_levanter.py`, `test_runner_models.py` beyond

#12310 also moves `printed_status` into `rl_tests/fixtures.py`, but its

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[mochi] Enable DSpark for one-rack RL (#12239)

Enable four-proposal DSpark for one-rack Mochi RL from the pinned
step-400407 initializer. The default uses the interleaved 766M two-layer
draft at a 0.775 vLLM memory fraction. Standard and agentic one-rack
presets inherit the setting. Three-rack presets use plain decoding
pending measurements at 262k context with FlashInfer.

Keep Speculators for draft fitting and Levanter for assistant masks.
Seeded sampling interleaves the SFT sources by sampled row count and
keeps the first-user prompt holdout. Both draft sizes share a prepared
dataset and teacher activations. Prefill once on the teacher gang, then
fit each draft as a checkpoint ArtifactStep on one GPU. The cache is
reusable for 48 hours from prefill start. Fitting publishes a
SkyRL-ready export and prints its source URI and identity.

### Five-update one-rack comparison

All three runs used Mochi step 400407, the same workload, and 60 GB200s.
Plain used a 0.75 memory fraction. Both drafts used four proposals and
0.775.

| Metric | Plain | Prior 521M | Interleaved 766M |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Startup before update 1 | 12m03s | 16m24s | 14m02s |
| Update 1 | 40m40s | 30m52s | 28m48s |
| Mean update, updates 2–3 | 4m38s | 2m22s | 2m16s |
| Update 5 | 14m59s | 16m24s | 9m46s |
| Total updates 2–5 | 34m18s | 27m21s | 21m32s |
| Median update, updates 2–5 | 7m47s | 4m18s | 4m47s |
| Successful rollout call p95, updates 2–5 | 23m17s | 15m23s | 15m20s |
| Lead GPU task wall time | 89m23s | 76m03s | 65m52s |

The 766M cut total warm update time by 37% versus plain and 21% versus
the prior draft. The two drafts had similar times in updates 2–3. On
update 5, rollout admission took 449 s with the 766M and 840 s with the
prior draft. Startup runs from lead GPU task start to the first
rollout-wait window. Task wall time excludes the scheduling queue. The
p95 pools successful rollout calls dispatched during updates 2–5.
[Five-update
analysis](https://loom.oa.dev/s/heul67oq/artifacts/mochi-dspark-performance)
· [Per-step
timings](https://loom.oa.dev/s/heul67oq/artifacts/mochi-dspark-step-time)

Warm trainer–vLLM mean absolute log ratios on fresh tokens were 0.00951,
0.00967, and 0.01033 for plain, 521M, and 766M. The arms had 488k, 358k,
and 243k fresh tokens respectively, so coverage differed. The 766M
reached 3.077 acceptance length on the shared holdout versus 2.759 for
the prior draft, with 119.4k KV tokens per GPU versus 132.2k. The
interleaved 521M was preempted twice before completing an RL update.
[Ablation
records](https://loom.oa.dev/s/heul67oq/artifacts/mochi-dspark-ablation)

### Use the draft on another branch

Use the permanent CoreWeave export with the step-400407 verifier and the
Nov 24 ShortConv vLLM wheel. Add these options to a one-rack Mochi
launch. [Draft
files](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-08a%2Fmarin%2Fcheckpoints%2Fdspark%2Fmochi%2Fablation-interleaved-two-layer%2F2026.11.25-skyrl)
· [Verifier
export](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8089#issuecomment-6841382920)
· [vLLM
wheel](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/releases/tag/marin-vllm-gpu-20261124-36cef9c0caf3)

--set 'generator.speculative_decoding={
  "method": "dspark",

  "model": {
    "source_uri": "s3://marin-us-east-08a/marin/checkpoints/dspark/mochi/ablation-interleaved-two-layer/2026.11.25-skyrl",

commits.author: ravwojdyla-agent
commits.message:
[finestore] Bound the memory of full-table reads and compaction (#12176)

Full-table reads and compaction merge every shard of a table in key
order and keep all of its shards open. Shards had row groups of up to
100 MB and the readers held a few of them per shard, so memory grew with
the shard count. On a 3.4M-row, 23 GB table, a full export and a
full-table column backfill were both killed at 128 GB.

Shards now get row groups of at most 4 MB of Arrow data, separate from
the 100 MB write buffer that sets when a table flushes. Ordered reads
(`iter_rows`) and compaction read a shard one row group at a time and
fetch later groups, up to 4 MB of them, on a thread pool, so each open
shard holds about two decoded groups. Ordered reads hand the merge
slices of about 1 MB. Shard files open with their manifest size and
without fsspec's 50 MiB read-ahead, so opening a shard once per row
group sends no HEAD request. The shared range cache fetches different
ranges of one file at once.

On CoreWeave S3 in the same region, one run, with 32 shards of 8,000
rows of 7 KB (1.8 GB of Arrow data, 454 MB of Parquet):

| Operation | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Ordered read, all shards spanning all keys | 9.7 s, 5,149 MB | 7.8 s,
325 MB |
| Ordered read, disjoint key ranges | 9.1 s, 1,885 MB | 9.2 s, 259 MB |
| Ordered read of the key column only | 1.0–1.3 s | 2.8–3.1 s |
| Unordered scan | 3.9 s | 2.0–2.2 s |
| Point lookup, overlapping / disjoint | 1,756 / 111 ms | 236 / 18 ms |
| Lookup of 2,000 keys | 3.1–3.2 s | 1.3 s |
| Compaction of the 32 overlapping shards | 19.0 s, 5,152 MB | 16.6 s,
772 MB |
| Write, 32 flushes | 38–41 s | 43–44 s |

Memory is peak Arrow allocation. The archive size does not change.
Across three runs, writes took 38–42 s before and 39–45 s after. The
key-column read is slower because a narrow projection needs one small
range request per row group, 14 times as many in this benchmark, and
Arrow's I/O pool runs at most 8 at a time.

Shards written before this change keep their 100 MB row groups until
compaction rewrites them, and `maintain()` never rewrites the top level.
An ordered read of such an archive took 1,784 MB here instead of 5,149
MB. A single compaction that rewrites a large existing table holds one
old row group, up to 100 MB, per input shard.

commits.author: ravwojdyla-agent
commits.message:
[finestore] Reject commits over rows changed after they were read (#12178)

Transaction.read returns the newest rows for the given primary keys from
the transaction's pinned snapshot and guards those keys. The commit
checks the guards in check_preconditions, next to the table guards that
require_unchanged adds (#12203), against each manifest a publication
attempt builds on, including retries after a HEAD conflict. If a guarded
key has a row committed after the transaction's snapshot, the commit
raises RowConflict instead of replacing it. Absent keys are guarded too,
so two transactions that insert the same new key conflict. A drop or
replacement of the guarded table raises CommitConflict. The check reuses
ReadView's keyed lookup, limited to shards that hold a row newer than
the snapshot.

DataStore.update(table, keys, edit, message=...) reads the rows, applies
edit and commits. On RowConflict it backs off with jitter and runs edit
again on the newer rows, up to 20 attempts, so edit must be safe to
repeat. It rejects missing keys, edits that change the primary key, and
tables that do not use OnConflict.SUPERSEDE.

Without the check, the later of two writers that read the same row
replaces the earlier edit without an error. In a 3.4M-row store, eight
writers making 80 read-modify-write edits to one row kept 10 of them.
With update, none was lost; 5 edits raised RowConflict after 20
attempts, in a run that retried without the backoff added here.

commits.author: yonromai
commits.message:
[skyrl] Require a spare prompt in each rollout pool (#12179)

Require one distinct prompt per open rollout slot and one spare in each
pool. Validate the count after dataset preparation, using each family's
quota when set. Skip a quarantine that would take the pool below its
minimum.

Quarantine cooldowns count completed batches. Keeping a spare leaves the
scheduler another candidate when a rejection and future batch
reservations
would otherwise leave the current batch waiting for a cooldown to
expire.

Repeat quarantine backoff follows in #12180.
